name: Fibonacci Words Solution
description:
Implement a complete solution for the Fibonacci Words problem.

The program reads test cases from stdin until EOF. Each test case consists of two lines: an integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 100) and a bit pattern p (up to 100,000 chars of '0' and '1'). For each test case, output how many times p occurs (with overlapping) in F(n), the n-th Fibonacci word defined by F(0)='0', F(1)='1', F(k)=F(k-1)+F(k-2) for k≥2.

Key algorithm: KMP for overlapping pattern matching combined with a DP recurrence tracking count, prefix, suffix, and length per Fibonacci level. For F(k)=F(k-1)+F(k-2), count(k)=count(k-1)+count(k-2)+cross_matches where cross_matches are new occurrences spanning the concatenation boundary. Python arbitrary-precision integers handle arbitrarily large counts.

types.name: FibState

fields.name: count
fields.description: Number of overlapping occurrences of the pattern in F(k). Non-negative, arbitrary precision.

fields.name: prefix
fields.description: The first min(len(F(k)), len(pattern)-1) characters of F(k). Used for cross-boundary matching when F(k) appears as the right part of a concatenation. Contains only '0' and '1'.

validators.error_message: Prefix must consist only of '0' and '1' characters

fields.name: suffix
fields.description: The last min(len(F(k)), len(pattern)-1) characters of F(k). Used for cross-boundary matching when F(k) appears as the left part of a concatenation. Contains only '0' and '1'.

validators.error_message: Suffix must consist only of '0' and '1' characters

fields.name: length
fields.description: The length of F(k), capped at 2 * len(pattern) for practical purposes. Once length exceeds this threshold, the exact value is irrelevant since prefix and suffix no longer overlap. Must be >= 1.

validators.error_message: Fibonacci word length must be at least 1

types.description: DP state for a single Fibonacci word level. Represents the accumulated occurrence count, the prefix and suffix fragments needed for cross-boundary matching, and the (capped) length of the Fibonacci word at that level.

types.name: FailureTable
types.description: The KMP failure (partial match / prefix) table. A list of non-negative integers of the same length as the pattern, where failure[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of pattern[0..i] that is also a suffix.

types.name: TestCase

validators.error_message: n must be between 0 and 100 inclusive

fields.name: pattern
fields.description: Bit pattern to search for, consisting of '0' and '1' characters, length 1 to 100000.

validators.error_message: Pattern length must be between 1 and 100000
Pattern must consist only of '0' and '1' characters

types.description: A single parsed test case consisting of the Fibonacci word index and the pattern to search for.

functions.name: build_failure_table
functions.description: Computes the KMP failure (prefix) function for the given pattern. failure[i] equals the length of the longest proper prefix of pattern[0..i] that is also a suffix of pattern[0..i]. This table is built once per test case and reused across all KMP searches for that pattern.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The search pattern consisting of '0' and '1' characters. Must have length >= 1.

validators.error_message: Pattern must consist only of '0' and '1' characters

error_data.message: Pattern must be non-empty for failure table construction

preconditions: all characters in pattern are '0' or '1'
postconditions: for all i in 0..len(pattern)-1: 0 <= result[i] <= i
for all i in 0..len(pattern)-1: pattern[0:result[i]] == pattern[i-result[i]+1:i+1]

structured_side_effects.description: Pure function with no side effects

functions.name: kmp_count_overlapping
functions.description: Counts all overlapping occurrences of pattern in text using the KMP algorithm with the precomputed failure table. After finding a match at position i, the search continues from the state indicated by failure[m-1] (where m = len(pattern)) to allow overlapping matches. Returns 0 immediately if len(text) < len(pattern).

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to search within. May be empty or shorter than the pattern.

validators.error_message: Text must consist only of '0' and '1' characters

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The search pattern. Must be non-empty.

inputs.name: failure
inputs.description: Precomputed KMP failure table for the pattern. Must have been built by build_failure_table(pattern).

error_data.message: Failure table length must match pattern length

postconditions: result equals the number of indices i such that text[i:i+len(pattern)] == pattern

structured_side_effects.description: Pure function with no side effects

performance_budget.complexity: O(n + m) where n = len(text), m = len(pattern)

functions.name: compute_cross_matches
functions.description: Computes the number of new pattern occurrences that span the concatenation boundary when F(k-1) and F(k-2) are joined to form F(k). Specifically: kmp_count_overlapping(suffix_prev + prefix_prev2, pattern, failure) - kmp_count_overlapping(suffix_prev, pattern, failure) - kmp_count_overlapping(prefix_prev2, pattern, failure). This isolates only the matches that genuinely cross the boundary and have not already been counted in either half. Pure convenience wrapper around kmp_count_overlapping.

inputs.name: suffix_prev
inputs.description: Suffix of F(k-1): the last min(len(F(k-1)), len(pattern)-1) characters. May be empty if pattern has length 1.

validators.error_message: Suffix must consist only of '0' and '1' characters
Suffix length must be at most len(pattern)-1 which is at most 99999

inputs.name: prefix_prev2
inputs.description: Prefix of F(k-2): the first min(len(F(k-2)), len(pattern)-1) characters. May be empty if pattern has length 1.

validators.error_message: Prefix must consist only of '0' and '1' characters
Prefix length must be at most len(pattern)-1 which is at most 99999

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The search pattern. Must be non-empty.

inputs.name: failure
inputs.description: Precomputed KMP failure table for the pattern.

error_data.message: Failure table length must match pattern length

postconditions: result == kmp_count_overlapping(suffix_prev + prefix_prev2, pattern, failure) - kmp_count_overlapping(suffix_prev, pattern, failure) - kmp_count_overlapping(prefix_prev2, pattern, failure)

structured_side_effects.description: Pure function with no side effects

performance_budget.complexity: O(m) where m = len(pattern), since suffix and prefix are each at most len(pattern)-1 chars

functions.name: solve
functions.description: Main solver for a single test case. Given the Fibonacci word index n and a pattern, returns the number of overlapping occurrences of pattern in F(n). Algorithm: (1) Build KMP failure table once. (2) Initialize base cases F(0)='0', F(1)='1' as FibState values. (3) Iterate from k=2 to n, computing count(k) = count(k-1) + count(k-2) + cross_matches. (4) Update prefix(k) and suffix(k) from the concatenation. Handles edge cases: if pattern is longer than F(n), returns 0; for n=0 and n=1, directly matches against the single-character strings.

inputs.name: n
inputs.description: Fibonacci word index. Must satisfy 0 <= n <= 100.

validators.error_message: n must be between 0 and 100 inclusive

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: Bit pattern to search for. Non-empty, consisting of '0' and '1', length 1 to 100000.

validators.error_message: Pattern length must be between 1 and 100000
Pattern must consist only of '0' and '1' characters

error_data.message: n must be between 0 and 100 inclusive

error_cases.name: invalid_pattern_chars
error_cases.condition: pattern contains characters other than '0' and '1'

error_data.message: Pattern must consist only of '0' and '1' characters

postconditions: result equals the number of overlapping occurrences of pattern in F(n)
for n=0: result == (1 if pattern == '0' else 0)
for n=1: result == (1 if pattern == '1' else 0)

structured_side_effects.description: Pure function with no side effects — all I/O is in main()

performance_budget.complexity: O(n * m) where n = Fibonacci index (up to 100), m = len(pattern) (up to 100000)

functions.name: main
functions.description: Entry point. Reads all input from stdin until EOF, parsing test cases as pairs of lines (integer n, then pattern string). For each test case numbered starting at 1, calls solve(n, pattern) and prints 'Case X: Y' to stdout where X is the 1-based case number and Y is the occurrence count. Each output line is terminated by a newline. Handles EOF gracefully via try/except or equivalent.

error_cases.name: eof_between_lines
error_cases.condition: EOF encountered after reading n but before reading pattern

error_data.message: Unexpected EOF: expected pattern line after n

error_cases.name: invalid_n_format
error_cases.condition: First line of a test case cannot be parsed as an integer

error_data.message: Could not parse n as an integer

preconditions: stdin contains zero or more valid test cases
each test case is two consecutive lines: first line is an integer 0..100, second line is a non-empty bit string of length 1..100000
postconditions: for each test case i (1-indexed), exactly one line 'Case {i}: {count}' is written to stdout
output lines are in the same order as input test cases
each output line is terminated by a newline character
side_effects: Reads all available input from stdin

structured_side_effects.description: Reads test cases from standard input until EOF
Writes 'Case X: Y' result lines to standard output

performance_budget.complexity: O(T * n * m) where T = number of test cases, n = max Fibonacci index, m = max pattern length

invariants: F(0) is defined as '0' and F(1) is defined as '1'
For k >= 2, F(k) = F(k-1) + F(k-2) (string concatenation)
The KMP failure table is built exactly once per test case and shared across all KMP invocations for that test case
Prefix and suffix strings stored in FibState have length at most len(pattern) - 1
FibState.length is capped at 2 * len(pattern); values beyond this threshold are treated as equivalent (sufficiently large)
count(k) = count(k-1) + count(k-2) + cross_matches for k >= 2
cross_matches = kmp_count(suffix(k-1) + prefix(k-2), p) - kmp_count(suffix(k-1), p) - kmp_count(prefix(k-2), p)
All pattern matching uses KMP with overlapping support — no regex or str.count()
solve() is a pure function with no I/O side effects
Output case numbering is 1-based and sequential
Python arbitrary-precision integers are used for counts; no overflow is possible
